THE PALETTE

Bone #FAF7F2 page, white cards, sand #F2ECE3 fills, taupe #E6DED2 rules, warm ink #241F1A. Nothing is pure grey — every neutral is warmed, which is what stops it reading as a generic admin panel.

Colour is rationed. KODE blue #2150A0 appears only on the mark and the single primary action. Status uses muted naturals rather than signal colours: sage #5F7A5A ready, ochre #B8862B attention, brick #A9524A stopped, clay #B0764F for scans and anything needing a claim.

THE TYPE

Instrument Serif for the greeting and every headline figure — it is what makes the dashboard feel considered rather than generated. Montserrat carries all interface text, so the brand's own typeface still does the work everywhere a person reads a label.

Serif is used sparingly and only for numbers and page titles. Used on body text it would read as a magazine, not a tool.

EVERY FIGURE IS REAL

All four tiles, the series and the fleet panel come from GET /stats/overview and the printer list — impressions, estimated cost in EGP, scans with an unclaimed count, sheets saved by duplex.

The two-line chart separates app jobs from walk-up use, because the backend refuses to call the second one printing.

The coverage note in the lower right is not decoration — it is coverageNote from the summary response, rendered where the totals are, in the same weight as everything else. A caveat behind a tooltip does not exist on a phone.

Walk-up rows say "Device activity", never "print", which is what the backend's walkupReportLabel is for.

The mobile view is the same information, re-ranked rather than re-designed: greeting and the print action first, four tiles in a 2×2, the chart compressed to a sparkline, and the fleet cut to the printers that need something.

The broken printer sorts to the top in both views.
